Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reinstated Amid Political Scrutiny and Market Surge

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was reinstated by the company's board after an 11-day absence, a move that coincided with a significant surge in Nvidia's stock price, leading to the largest single-day gain for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite since April 2025. The reinstatement followed revelations of an extramarital affair by Huang with a woman suspected of passing information to Chinese intelligence services. US House Committees have stated that Huang's return does not erase security concerns, and both Republican and Democratic senators have objected to the circumstances of his reinstatement and alleged intervention by President Trump. Reports suggest Trump's own business stakes in Nvidia may have benefited from the company's stock rebound. The board reportedly reversed its decision to remove Huang after pressure from markets and officials, including President Trump, who cited national security concerns and US leadership in AI. Huang had disclosed additional affairs to the board prior to his reinstatement.
